title: Density Matrices and Noise
summary: Mixed states, Kraus channels, and why the error probability is not the wrong-answer probability.
mission: The circuit H, T, T†, H returns |0⟩. Between T and T†, insert an error: X with probability p_x, Z with probability p_z, nothing otherwise. Compute the final density matrix and store in p_wrong the probability of measuring 1 and in purity the purity Tr(ρ²), for p_x = p_z = 0.2.

prediction.question: With p_x = p_z = 0.2, the error happens in 40% of the runs. With what probability does the final measurement give the wrong result (1)?
prediction.explanation: After the final H, a Z error becomes a full X: it always flips the result. An X error between T and T†, on the other hand, becomes a rotation that flips the result only half the time. Total: 0.2 + 0.2 × 0.5 = 30%.

hints: A channel is given by Kraus operators. For this error: √(1 − p_x − p_z)·I, √p_x·X and √p_z·Z. Build this list in error_kraus and apply it with qml.QubitChannel(error_kraus(p_x, p_z), wires=0).
The circuit is qml.Hadamard, qml.T, the channel, qml.adjoint(qml.T(wires=0)) and qml.Hadamard. To keep ρ, the device must be default.mixed and the QNode returns qml.density_matrix(wires=0).
With rho = circuit(p_x, p_z), the probability of measuring 1 is rho[1, 1] and the purity is np.trace(rho @ rho). Use np.real to keep the real part.

messages.ok: Density matrix correct for all the error probabilities tested. Wrong answer in {p_wrong} of the runs and purity {purity}: the noise left the state mixed.
